Made the minds snapshot-image producer (`scripts/snapshot_minds_e2e_state.py`) wait for the workspace's deferred install (the env.d browser unit that apt-installs Xvfb and the Fortress engine) before stopping the container and snapshotting. Previously the snapshot raced the background install: a build that lost the race minted a snapshot whose xvfb service could never spawn, so `test_backup_restore_rewinds_the_resumed_workspace_in_place` failed on every retry of that CI run (all attempts share the one snapshot) while other runs stayed green. The wait is bounded at 5 minutes (the install runs concurrently with the multi-minute create, so the residual wait is normally seconds) and fails the build loudly on timeout instead of minting a broken snapshot; the bound fits inside the existing 25-minute exec timeout's headroom, so a slow install fails with the wait's diagnostic error rather than a generic exec timeout. The in-sandbox runner program string is now compile-checked by a unit test, so a syntax error in it fails at unit-test time instead of after the multi-minute image build in CI.
